open_decisions.question: Which character encoding (code page) do the files and areas described by these copybooks use for DISPLAY data on the legacy platform (EBCDIC 037, 1140, another EBCDIC variant, or ASCII)? The zoned-decimal test vectors and String codecs depend on it.

BR-120 (SME review): 'VAL-NUMERIC-CHECK IS NOT NUMERIC' after MOVE LS-INPUT-VALUE(5:4) TO VAL-NUMERIC-CHECK (PIC X(10)); the 6 padded spaces make the test true for every input, so as written no portfolio ID can pass ('LS-RETURN-CODE = VAL-INVALID-ID; error message'). The source comment says the ID 'must start with PORT and have 4 numeric digits'. What is the intended portfolio-ID suffix rule (length and content), and is the defect known in production?

BR-121 (SME review): 'LS-INPUT-VALUE IS NOT NUMERIC OR LS-INPUT-VALUE = ZEROS' -> 'LS-RETURN-CODE = VAL-INVALID-ACCT; error message'. The NUMERIC test covers the whole 50-character input, so a 10-digit account number followed by spaces is rejected, although the source comment says 'Account number must be 10 numeric digits'. What is the intended account-number length and rule?

BR-123 (SME review): 'VAL-TEMP-NUM < VAL-MIN-AMOUNT OR VAL-TEMP-NUM > VAL-MAX-AMOUNT' -> 'LS-RETURN-CODE = VAL-INVALID-AMT'. PORTVAL declares VAL-MIN-AMOUNT -9999999999999.99 and VAL-MAX-AMOUNT +9999999999999.99, the full S9(13)V99 range, so no valid number is rejected; the alphanumeric-to-numeric MOVE of non-digit input is compiler-dependent. What are the intended minimum and maximum amounts, and how must non-numeric input be treated?
